CanonicalKeywords.rationale: `{ CardKeyword.Unplayable, CardKeyword.Retain }` (PoorSleep.cs:12-16) == both flags, and the RETAIN is the whole curse: an unplayable card that the end-of-turn hand flush will not discard, so it clogs the hand for the rest of the combat. As a CANONICAL keyword it carries no downgrade-rebuild hazard, unlike card/gold_axe's and card/wish's upgrade-added Retain.

ctor.issue: CURSE / CURSE / NONE map exactly. The canonical energy cost is -1 in C# and 0 in the sim. `CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers` returns early on `_base < 0` (CardEnergyCost.cs:100-103), so the game's unplayable card is immune to every cost modifier; the sim runs a base of 0 through the full modifier chain (cards/base.py:222-232). Only what is READ diverges. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/ascenders_bane's ctor entry (rule 3). DORMANT: every ported cost reader filters `> 0` or skips `<= 1`, and events/infested_automaton.py:35 filters pool_card_ids(), which holds no curses.

OnPlay.rationale: PoorSleep.cs has no members beyond the three overrides -- no OnPlay, no OnTurnEndInHand, no vars. Its whole effect is the keyword pair.

guards.what: the sim adds `is_unpowered = True` (poor_sleep.py:156), which has no counterpart in PoorSleep.cs
guards.rationale: Inert: the flag only steers `DamageCmd.deal`'s prop inference and the card deals no damage.
